evidence.claim: Cape to Cape links Atlantic beaches and back bays with the inland towns of Berlin and Snow Hill.
evidence.quote: The Cape to Cape Scenic Byway provides access to sites along the Atlantic Ocean and its back bays in Worcester County, running between Ocean City and the Virginia border south of Snow Hill.

evidence.claim: Maryland’s tourism office describes a 79-mile scenic drive on local and state roads, with five to seven hours allowed.
evidence.quote: 79 miles From bay to ocean along the Atlantic Coast on local and state roads Drive Time 5-7 hours

evidence.claim: Its highlights range from Berlin’s red-brick buildings to Assateague’s undeveloped barrier shore and free-roaming horses.
evidence.quote: Assateague Island , an undeveloped, 37-mile-long barrier island

evidence.claim: The byway was originally the eastern part of the Blue Crab Scenic Byway.
evidence.quote: The Cape to Cape Scenic Byway was originally the eastern portion of the Blue Crab Scenic Byway.

evidence.claim: Parts of its course are much older: modern MD 12 generally follows the post road from Snow Hill south to Virginia.
evidence.quote: the post road from Snow Hill south to Virginia (whose track is generally followed by modern Maryland Route 12)

evidence.claim: At Stockton, that route met a road linking a Pocomoke River landing with Chincoteague Bay, where small seagoing vessels could anchor.
evidence.quote: with the road from Mattapony Landing on the Pocomoke River to the Chincoteague Bay (the eastern part of which is now Maryland Route 366), where small ocean-going vessels could drop anchor.

evidence.claim: Travel north from the Virginia line through Stockton to Snow Hill, at the head of navigation on the Pocomoke.
evidence.quote: From Snow Hill, the byway follows MD 12 south to the Virginia border

evidence.claim: Continue to Berlin, then turn east on MD 376 toward the MD 611 branch for Assateague Island.
evidence.quote: The Cape to Cape Scenic Byway heads west along MD 376 to Berlin

evidence.claim: The Verrazano Bridge carries the island approach across Sinepuxent Bay.
evidence.quote: The Verrazano Bridge is a bridge on Maryland Route 611 over Sinepuxent Bay that connects Assateague Island to the mainland.

evidence.claim: Back on the mainland, the route continues toward Ocean City via US 50, ending among the resort’s beaches and boardwalk.
evidence.quote: From here, the Cape to Cape Scenic Byway heads south on MD 528, west on US 50 and south on MD 611, with a branch heading to Assateague Island

evidence.claim: Fires in 1844 and 1893 destroyed the center, including successive courthouses.
evidence.quote: Major fires in 1844 and 1893 destroyed the center of Snow Hill, including two successive court houses

evidence.claim: Some eighteenth-century buildings survived both, but rapid rebuilding after the second fire left many commercial buildings from the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
evidence.quote: but some 18th-century structures survived both fires. Following the second fire, much of the commercial area was rapidly rebuilt, so the downtown today contains many historic buildings of the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

evidence.claim: It became a port of entry in 1694 and the Worcester County seat in 1742.

evidence.claim: Municipal parks now provide boat landings and dockage.

evidence.claim: the Worcester County seat in 1742.
evidence.quote: In 1742, Worcester County was carved out of the eastern half of old Somerset County and Snow Hill, centrally located in the new county and at the head of navigation on the Pocomoke River, was made the county seat.

evidence.claim: Main Street follows a former post road to Philadelphia, at the crossroads where Berlin developed in the early nineteenth century.
evidence.quote: the Burley Plantation became a crossroads of a post road leading to Philadelphia (today's Main Street) and the Sinepuxent Road. Berlin developed in the early-19th century at this crossroads

evidence.claim: A fire in 1895 destroyed much of the commercial center; rebuilding brought Queen Anne, Italianate and Second Empire details to its Victorian buildings.
evidence.quote: After a fire in 1895 leveled a significant portion of the central commercial district, Victorian structures displaying elements of Queen Anne, Italianate, and Second Empire styles were erected along Main Street.

evidence.claim: Those streets later took on another identity for Runaway Bride in 1999, when Main Street and nearby areas became the fictional Hale, Maryland.
evidence.quote: For Runaway Bride (1999), starring Richard Gere and Julia Roberts, Berlin's Main Street and some of the outlying areas were altered to become the fictional town of Hale, Maryland.

evidence.claim: The historic downtown has undergone revitalization since the late 1980s.
evidence.quote: Since the late 1980s, the town has undergone considerable revitalization of its historic downtown commercial district and adjacent residential areas.

evidence.claim: Assateague’s barrier shore once carried plans for development, with a paved road called Baltimore Boulevard.
evidence.quote: In 1950, a 15-mile section of the Maryland side of Assateague was plotted for development, and a paved road, Baltimore Boulevard, was constructed to traverse the new development.

evidence.claim: The Ash Wednesday Storm of 1962 destroyed or buried most of that road and wrecked many island structures.
evidence.quote: The Ash Wednesday Storm of 1962 destroyed or covered most of Baltimore Boulevard, and many of the structures on the island were destroyed.

evidence.claim: Maryland then generally supported a national seashore, which Congress established in 1965.
evidence.quote: by this time the state of Maryland generally supported a national seashore and legislation was introduced in the United States Congress.

evidence.claim: Feral horses live on the island, with fencing at the state boundary separating the Maryland and Virginia herds.
evidence.quote: The Maryland and Virginia horses are kept apart by fencing at the border between the two states.

evidence.claim: The two sides also have separate road approaches; no road runs the island’s full length.
evidence.quote: Bridge access for cars is possible from both Maryland and Virginia, though no road runs the full north-south length of the island.

evidence.claim: which Congress established in 1965.
evidence.quote: new legislation in 1965 was successful and Assateague Island National Seashore was formed.

evidence.claim: Snow Hill’s municipal parks provide landings for boats

evidence.quote: At Porter's Crossing it turns southwest, broadening into a slow meandering river, flowing past the town of Snow Hill

evidence.claim: Rail service after the Civil War made Berlin a commercial center, while Ocean City’s growth later brought travelers through as a rest stop.

evidence.claim: Ocean City’s growth later brought travelers through as a rest stop.
evidence.quote: The rise of nearby Ocean City as a tourist destination in the early-twentieth century also aided Berlin's economy by making the town a convenient rest stop.

evidence.quote: The Maryland horses are owned and managed by the NPS, who have carefully followed the population over generations. In Virginia, the Chincoteague ponies are owned by the Chincoteague Volunteer Fire Company.
